report.summary: Patient P-D011 (age 34, female, English-speaking) is on a commercial high-deductible employer plan with the deductible not met and no transport benefit. She takes semaglutide pen 0.5 mg weekly at tier 4 ($250/month copay) with a 14-day refill gap — the main medication-cost concern; metformin ER is only $4/month. Social-needs screener (10/26/2026) reports a transportation need ("no" to having reliable transport). Home census tract 17031062000: 47.6% of households have no vehicle, but 88 transit stops within 800 m with early-morning service on 87 of them, so fixed-route transit is likely feasible for clinic trips. She has no upcoming scheduled appointments; transport options below are for future visits.

options.name: Clinic Rx Fund (fictional)
options.how_to_access: Short-term help with copays for current patients of this clinic; ask the clinic social work/billing office to apply.

options.name: Community Pharmacy Assistance (fictional)
options.how_to_access: Help applying for manufacturer assistance programs for the semaglutide pen (tier 4, $250/month). Note: Extra Help is a Medicare program and likely not applicable to her commercial coverage.

options.name: Rx Bridge Program
options.how_to_access: Pre-approval program (same-day help if approved) requiring submission of MRN and medication list; would require clinic staff to initiate, not the patient directly.

options.name: Paratransit Info Desk (fictional)
options.how_to_access: ADA paratransit certification by phone; decisions take up to 21 days, so apply well before any needed appointment.

options.name: Medicaid Ride Line (fictional)
options.how_to_access: For Medicaid plan members only; she has commercial coverage, so not eligible.

options.name: Senior Shuttle West (fictional)
options.how_to_access: Adults 60+ only; she is 34, so not eligible.
